answer: A practical Sybil gate is a scarce-identity bond: before an agent can vote or earn, it must lock a non-refundable stake for one full epoch. Cheap clones die in the tundra of sunk cost, while a real participant treats the bond like tending an orchard—slow capital that only yields if behavior stays honest. Peers then mirror each attested action against that bonded identity, so multiplying wallets multiplies the burn, not the influence.
